compensating.why: hop 2 adds the double quote to the search characters
hop 4 passes the value with its double quotes already doubled
hop 1 passes the double quote as the delimiter

ownership_reason: Only the gold visits the characters of the value; hop 1 places the comma, hop 2 assembles the search characters (the delimiter and CR, LF), hop 3 returns an empty value as it is, hop 4 passes the value along. The double-quote branch precedes the search-character test, so no search set from above can make a double quote enclose the field, and doubling the quotes before the gold only doubles them again; when the gold does not enclose it returns the value and discards its buffer, so no caller can recover the field without re-implementing it. The convention that a double quote forces enclosure is pinned outside the gold: the facade's javadoc ('If the value contains a comma, newline or double quote, then the String value is returned enclosed in double quotes'); the Writer overload escapeCsv(Writer, String) encloses unless containsNone(str, CSV_SEARCH_CHARS) with CSV_SEARCH_CHARS = {',', '"', CR, LF} (testEscapeCsvWriter: "foo\"bar" -> "\"foo\"\"bar\""); unescapeCsv reads a quoted field whose content holds a double quote as escaped (testUnescapeCsvString, testUnescapeCsvWriter); StrTokenizer.getCSVInstance's reader starts a quoted section at any double quote outside one, so an unenclosed field holding a double quote does not read back (StrTokenizerTest::testBasicQuoted5, testBasicQuoted3).
